Hi Jessica —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of requirements (what I heard)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 250ms (you mentioned 200–250ms range on the call)
- First chunk / first token: ideally <= 200ms for interactive flows
- Chunk cadence for streaming: target ~100–200ms per chunk (SSE or WebSocket)
- Concurrency: expected peak ~300 concurrent requests, average ~150
- Throughput: sustained pages of traffic ~500–800 tokens/sec during busy windows
- Payloads: avg prompt ~60–80 tokens, worst-case prompt ~1,200 tokens (batching allowed)

What we can do next
1) Validation run: we can run your sample payloads through our TTFT harness (attached: redwood-ttft-fixture-results.csv is a template with baseline numbers). If you share a representative sample payload set (or point us to the file you dropped on Drive), we can run a dedicated benchmark on a matching instance type and model variant.
2) Streaming mode: we support both SSE and WebSocket. From a TTFT perspective WebSocket has slight advantage for the handshake phase on long-lived connections; SSE is fine if you prefer server-initated events. We'll include chunk cadence tuning (we can target <150ms cadence for typical responses).
3) Model/quantization: for your latency targets we recommend a 13B-class model with int8 quantization as a starting point; we can also test 7B if quality allows.
4) Next meeting: propose a 60-min technical sync to review the benchmarking plan and expected traffic profile. Marissa and Ethan from our side will join.

Can you confirm the TTFT and chunk cadence targets above (I left the TTFT target as the broader range you mentioned)? Also please attach a small set of representative sample prompts (or share a Drive link) and any IP/data residency notes we should consider for the bench.

I’ll schedule the tech sync once I get a confirmation of targets and sample payloads.

Thanks,

Thanks Aditya — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: our goal is TTFT <= 250ms end-to-end for the majority of interactive calls. The strict SLA is first token <= 200ms for our highest tier customers; anything <250ms is acceptable for baseline users.
- Chunk cadence: we want chunks roughly every 100–200ms. Lower is fine but we don't need sub-50ms pacing.
- Streaming transport: preference is WebSocket (we have long-lived connections and want bidirectional control), but SSE would be OK for initial testing.
- Concurrency: prepare for peaks up to 300 concurrent connections; steady-state ~150.
- Model payloads: average prompt ~64 tokens; worst-case up to 1,024 tokens (we trimmed earlier estimate).

I've uploaded a small set of sample payloads to the Acme folder on Drive and attached one example to this thread (acme-sample-payload.json) for your bench. Also, please note we need to confirm data residency / SOC2 evidence as part of procurement.

2) Can you propose a bench run plan (approx duration, hardware profile) so we can clear it with infra?

Hi Jessica — great, thanks for the payloads and the clarifications. Answers and a proposed bench plan below.

SSE vs WebSocket for TTFT
- WebSocket: typically slightly lower TTFT for persistent connections because TLS + HTTP upgrade happens once; subsequent requests avoid handshake overhead. For your long-lived-connection use-case we recommend WebSocket for best steady-state TTFT.
- SSE: simpler to operate and fine for stateless short-lived calls; TTFT difference is usually <30–60ms but can vary with load and connection churn.

Recommended model and hardware
- Start: LlamaX-13B (int8 quantized) on an A100-class instance under our Dedicated pool for predictable p99 latency. Expected TTFT (first token) 140–220ms depending on prompt size and batching policies.
- Fallback: LlamaX-7B if you need lower-cost footprint; expect TTFT 100–200ms but quality may vary.

Bench plan (proposed)
- Goal: validate first-token latency and chunk cadence at concurrency points: 50, 150, 300.
- Duration: 20–30 minutes per concurrency step (warm-up 5 mins + 15–25 mins measurement). Total ~90 minutes.
- Payloads: use the acme-sample-payload.json you attached (we'll run the set across the distribution you provided).
- Metrics: TTFT (median/p95/p99), chunk cadence distribution, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and observed tail due to batching.
- Hardware profile: 1x A100-80GB for baseline runs. If we need more headroom we can spin a 2-GPU config.
- Deliverable: CSV with per-request latencies, aggregated SLO table, and recommended config for Dedicated pool.

What I'll run for you before the tech sync
- Quick run using your sample payloads on our harness to provide a baseline (I’ll attach a short results summary).
- Tune streaming chunk sizes / cadence to target ~120ms cadence and measure TTFT impact.

Next steps
- I'll run the bench tomorrow (Wed) morning PT and share the raw CSV + a short one-page summary (attachment: redwood-ttft-plan.pdf).
- Let's lock a 60-min tech sync to go through the results. Proposed times: Thu 09/14 10:00AM PT or Thu 09/14 3:00PM PT. Which works for you?

If you want, we can also include a short run that emulates ephemeral (non-persistent) connections to show SSE performance differences.
